graphEvents.label: Multi-target doctor commands collide on derived ids

label: Command admission has exactly two inputs: a per-skill command-metadata.json or an allow-list.json entry; only three skills carry metadata today, yielding 19 entries.
Command metadata requires command and ownerMode but carries description, argumentHint, userIntent.job, userIntent.ownedSignals, choreography and discriminator fields usable for plain-word routing.
Allow-list entries require id, command, skillId, ownerMode and reason, and cover commands whose owner skill has no command-metadata.json yet.

Bridge ids are command-derived and must match ^/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[a-z0-9-]+$ with explicit uniqueness; /doctor:git targets would collide at command-doctor-git, so doctor admission needs one bridge per command or non-derived allow-list ids.
routingEnabled is per-platform from scoring-compatibility.json; the generator emits signal lists only for enabled runtimes, with 5 TypeScript-active and 15 Python-active bridges.
The Python harvester roots at .skilled/skills and reads doc frontmatter only from references/ and assets/ subdirectories when building its signal map.
The TS harvester mirrors the references/assets scope over markdown files and is gated by SPECKIT_ADVISOR_DOC_TRIGGERS.
Harvested doc triggers land in the skill_docs table with content-hash upsert/delete and reach scoring through the derived lane with a top-3-doc, 0.45-capped contribution.

Neither supported mechanism can consume _routes.yaml directly (wrong root and file type for harvesters; no route granularity in bridges), so doctor routing requires authored metadata rather than manifest harvesting.
Any admission change must satisfy the command-bridges drift guard and the doctor route-validate.sh assertion.
